description: Use Cornacchia's Euclidean remainder descent to find the positive representation p=x^2+2y^2 from a supplied square root of -2 modulo prime p.

source.title: Remarks on the Algorithms of Cornacchia and Hermite-Serret; Quattro Formaggi, section 4.2.3
source.author: Jesse Ira Deutsch; Alexander Munch-Hansen
source.reference: Deutsch, JP Journal of Algebra, Number Theory and Applications 53(2), 2022, Theorem 1; Munch-Hansen, Quattro Formaggi, section 4.2.3.
source.implementation_status: Clean-room fixed-d=2 Cornacchia profile; source descriptions only.

contract.descent: Initialize previous=prime and current=root. Apply Euclidean remainders until current <= floor(sqrt(prime)); the final current is x.
contract.recovery: Compute y^2=(prime-x^2)/2. Return the packed pair only if this is a positive exact square and x^2+2*y^2=prime.
contract.deterministic_root: The unique square root of -2 in [1,prime/2] is supplied in the frame; the implementation validates it and never computes a modular square root.
contract.square_root_arithmetic: All square-root bounds use integer binary search; no floating-point arithmetic is used.
contract.prime_validation: Trial division checks odd primality through divisor <= prime/divisor; it avoids a squared-divisor overflow.
contract.packing: Since x<=999 and y<=707, y is below base 1024 and the packed scalar decodes without collisions.
contract.invalid_cases: Null, malformed, composite/even/out-of-range p, noncanonical root, or a root not congruent to -2 modulo p returns -1.

complexity.time: O(sqrt(p) + log(p)^2) integer operations including bounded trial primality validation; Cornacchia's Euclidean descent itself takes O(log p) divisions.
